The idea in brief Stimulus control therapy fixes insomnia by retraining your brain to associate the bed only with sleep.
You do this by going to bed only when sleepy, leaving the bed if you’re awake, and waking up at the same time every day.
If the bed becomes a place for thinking, scrolling, or trying to force sleep, it slowly turns into a space of alertness.
This is why you may feel sleepy elsewhere but suddenly awake when you lie down.
The core method Go to bed only when truly sleepy.
Engage in something quiet and low-stimulation, then return only when sleepiness builds again.
You might get out of bed multiple times or feel more tired during the day.
